summary: Ruth Gamble is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her BA from RMIT University and a PhD at Australian National University under John Powers, Roger R. Jackson, and David Templeman, holding posts at ANU, Munich, and La Trobe University.
Ruth Norton Albright was an Indologist who studied under Maurice Bloomfield at Johns Hopkins University, earning her PhD around 1916–1921.

Ruth W. Dunnell works in Sinology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her PhD at Princeton University in 1983, studied under Jinbo Shi, and served as James P. Storer Associate Professor at Kenyon College.
Ryan Anningson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under doctoral supervisor Jason Neelis (attested 2017).
Ryan Damron is an Indology scholar who was affiliated with the University of California, Berkeley as a graduate student (attested 2011) and doctoral candidate (attested 2020).

Ryan Matthew Jacobson is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned an MA in Religious Studies at Naropa University. He studied under instructors including Judith Simmer-Brown, David Phillip Stanley, and Sarah Harding, along with several traditional teachers.

Ryan Richard Overbey, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, earned degrees from Brown and Harvard. He held posts at Berkeley, College of the Holy Cross, Heidelberg Academy, Wesleyan University, and Skidmore College.
Ryo Kuroiwa works in computational fields and Indology, holding posts at the National Institute of Informatics and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.
Ryo Nishimura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Tohoku University around 1991–2000 and under Fumihiko Sueki around 1995–2004.
Ryōshō Taira was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Taisho University, where he was attested as professor emeritus in 1976 and attested again in 1984.
Ryodo Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar who held lecturer posts at Taisho University (attested 2015–2026) and Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryogon Fukuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and Humboldt University of Berlin under Ryotai Hatani, Ryujo Yamada, and Shun'ichi Takagi. He lectured at Humboldt and was a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1963–1974).
Ryoichi Kondo was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

Ryoji Kishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who held part-time lecturer posts attested in 2026 at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ryojin Soga was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Shinshu and Otani universities under Manshi Kiyozawa. He was a professor at Toyo University and served multiple professorships and as 17th president (1961–1967) at Otani University.
Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who held professorships at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and Rissho University (attested 2001).
Ryokei Kaginushi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who served as a professor at Otani University, attested in 1978 and 1993.
Ryoken Nawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who was an appointed researcher at Kyoto Koka Women's University (attested 2015) and a lecturer at Osaka University (attested 2020–2026).
Ryoko Mochizuki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo until 1963 and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1972 and 1983).

Ryosaburo Sakaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo under Karl Florenz and Alfred Foucher. He taught at Ryukoku University, Third Higher School, and became a professor at Kyoto University in 1908.
